topics.title: Rectangles, squares and why perimeter is not area

concepts.learning_objective: Find the area of a rectangle and of the triangles cut off by its diagonal using length x width.
Explain with examples why perimeter cannot be used as a measure of area.
Find the area of a path around or across a rectangular plot by subtracting or adding rectangles.

topics.title: Area of a triangle
topics.ncert_sections: Triangles; Some Applications of the Area Formula

concepts.learning_objective: Use area of a triangle = 1/2 x base x height for any triangle.
Find an unknown altitude by writing the area of a triangle with two different base-height pairs.
Use the fact that a line from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side halves the area of a triangle.

topics.title: Triangles between parallel lines with a common base
topics.ncert_sections: Triangles between Parallel Lines with a Common Base

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that triangles on the same base between the same parallels have equal areas.
Use reflection in a line to find the triangle of least perimeter on a given base.
Find the area of a polygon by dividing it into triangles.
Find the area of a quadrilateral from a diagonal and the perpendiculars dropped on it.
Use area of a parallelogram = base x corresponding height.
Explain how a parallelogram is dissected into a rectangle of equal area.
Use area of a rhombus = 1/2 x product of its diagonals.

topics.title: Trapezium
topics.ncert_sections: Trapezium; Finding the Area Using Two Copies of the Trapezium

concepts.learning_objective: Use area of a trapezium = 1/2 x height x sum of the parallel sides.
Explain how two copies of a trapezium form a parallelogram and give the area formula.
Convert between units of length and area such as in, cm, ft, in2 and cm2.
Compute and estimate areas of everyday objects such as an A4 sheet.
